query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Enhancing the boronizing treatment by increasing its temperature and duration will produce a thicker, denser boride layer that better inhibits molten aluminum penetration and thus improves the corrosion resistance of components used in hot‐dip aluminum‐plating equipment.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components processed under standard boronizing parameters that yield a relatively thin, conventional boride layer.
generation.intervention: Apply an optimized boronizing treatment with higher temperature and longer duration to promote thicker MB-type and M2B-type boride phase formation.
generation.conditions: Exposed in molten aluminum at typical hot-dip plating temperatures (~660 °C) under normal atmospheric conditions encountered during plating.
generation.structural_mediator: A thicker, well-adherent, low-defect boride surface layer (composed of MB-type and M2B-type borides).
generation.mechanism: The intensified boronizing reaction produces a continuous diffusion barrier that inhibits aluminum from reacting with the substrate, thereby preventing interdiffusion and corrosive dissolution in the molten aluminum environment.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated components will exhibit a lower corrosion rate in molten aluminum along with increased surface hardness compared to those processed with conventional boronizing parameters, ultimately extending component service life.
generation.baseline: Components receiving standard boronizing treatment, which form thinner boride layers and show higher rates of molten-aluminum induced corrosion.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects may decrease if the boride layer becomes excessively thick or brittle, or if variations in aluminum composition and plating process conditions fall outside typical operational parameters.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement is uncertain and may depend on the substrate composition and fine-tuning of processing parameters; further optimization is needed to determine the best balance between layer thickness and mechanical integrity.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of boride-based components: one group processed under standard boronizing conditions and a second group treated with an optimized higher temperature/longer duration boronizing process. Subject both sets to immersion in molten aluminum at ~660 °C for a fixed duration under identical conditions.
measurements: Corrosion weight loss per unit area
Microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM) to assess layer continuity and thickness
Depth profiling of aluminum diffusion into the substrate
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized treatment group does not show a statistically significant improvement in corrosion resistance (lower weight loss, reduced aluminum diffusion) and/or surface hardness compared to the standard treatment group, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Effect of Boronizing on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of CoCrFeNiMn High-Entropy Alloy

Abstract: AbstractThe CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloys were treated by powder-pack boriding to improve their surface hardness and wear resistance. The variation of boriding layer thickness with time and temperature was studied. Then, the frequency factor D0 and diffusion activation energy Q of element B in HEA are calculated to be 9.15 × 10−5 m2/s and 206.93 kJ/mol, respectively. The diffusion behavior of elements in the boronizing process was investigated and shows that the boride layer forms with the metal atoms diffusing outward and the diffusion layer forms with the B atoms diffusing inward by the Pt-labeling method. In addition, the surface microhardness of CoCrFeNiMn HEA was significantly improved to 23.8 ± 1.4 Gpa, and the friction coefficient was reduced from 0.86 to 0.48~0.61.Keywords: high entropy alloy, boronizing, growth kinetics, boronizing mechanism, wear resistance
